name: p1-tool-runtime
title: sub: p1-tool-runtime
creator: codex
notes: P1c complete: S1 (catalogue, PR #591), S2 (Gateway, PR #592), S3a/b/c-1/c-2/d (migration, PR #593-#597), S4 (L1 tool-schema producer, PR #598), S5 (gate + docs, this branch). S5 adds a static audit of the agent layer (backend/tools/runtime/audit.py + scripts/gates/tool_runtime_gate.py, run as its own CI job) and docs/tool-runtime.md. The audit is AST-only by design: importing an agent module would execute its imports and module-level wiring, and a gate must not have side effects (same rule as scan_declared_prompts). It checks four things -- an agent must not import a tool implementation (runtime types are fine; only base.py may import the bridge), its tool_capabilities declaration must match its invocation literals in both directions, anything it cannot read is a failure rather than a skip (non-literal capabilities, unknown shapes, unparseable sources -- that last rule came from a fixture bug that made the gate print 'clean' over a tree it never read), and catalogue coverage (unknown fails, orphan reports -- xhs.publish is the one orphan until P2a). The gate's own first rule was too strict and it flagged three legitimate imports on its author (ErrorKind / ToolResult / ToolGateway-in-TYPE_CHECKING); the boundary is now 'no tool objects', documented at _ALLOWED_PREFIX along with the fact that it was once drawn wrong. Scope is deliberately backend/agents/** only: the ripple-retry route in backend/api/routes/workflow.py:~2184 still calls RippleService directly on purpose. Next: P2a (publisher path + account credentials + policy engine) and P2c (LLM tool-calling, which is when BaseAgent.include_tool_schema gets flipped per agent).
